nodes.beat: Up among the rafters, which were spears laid side by side, Elsie could see the whole hall at once: the long fires, the benches, hundreds of warriors, the goat's mead going round in horns. At the far end, on the high seat, a man in a wide hat sat with one eye and two wolves at his feet, and he did not eat. Muninn went very still. It remembered him, it said. It remembered him so hard that it could not say anything else.

choices.gist: Tu te lèves, parce que tout le monde te regarde de toute façon.
choices.echo: Elsie se leva, et tous les visages du Valhalla se tournèrent avec elle.

nodes.beat: Elsie sat at the end of a bench with Muninn on her shoulder and ate boar, which was better than it had any right to be. The warriors on either side of her told the stories of their deaths as if they were funny, which mostly they were. Halfway through, the man on the high seat stood up. The hall went quiet, bench by bench, all the way down, and he looked straight at her.

choices.echo: Elsie recula, un pas, puis un autre, et la porte se mit à plier.

nodes.beat: The howl came again, and this time it was not far off: it was at the doors. Something huge and grey pressed its nose to the west door, and the carved wolf over it seemed to shrink. The warriors nearest the door stood up and reached for their shields. Sköll had followed the stone all the way here, and he was not going to wait outside.

nodes.role: the last square before it, and the way down is open

choices.gist: Tu descends les marches sous la grande salle, d'où vient l'odeur des chevaux, et où le noir est tiède.
choices.echo: Elsie descendit dans le noir, et le bruit de la grande salle s'étouffa au-dessus de sa tête.

choices.gist: Tu marches droit au milieu de la salle, devant tout le monde, la pierre à la main.
choices.echo: Elsie s'avança sur le sol à découvert, et toute la salle la regarda faire.

choices.gist: Tu fais le tour le long du mur, sous les boucliers suspendus, dans l'ombre, par le chemin le plus long.
choices.echo: Elsie se glissa dans l'ombre sous le mur, et la lumière du feu passa à côté d'elle.

nodes.beat: The west door burst open and Sköll came into Valhalla, grey and enormous, and the fires bent away from him. The warriors went for their shields. The one-eyed man on the high seat did not move at all; he was watching Elsie, to see what she would do. Between her and him lay the whole length of the hall: the open floor down the middle where everybody would see her, the wall of hanging shields along the side in shadow, and close by her feet a trapdoor standing open, with steps going down under the hall and a smell of horses.

nodes.role: below, where what was left is still waiting

choices.gist: Tu remontes hors du noir sur Sleipnir.
choices.echo: Sleipnir monta les marches comme si ce n'était rien, entra dans la grande salle et s'agenouilla pour la déposer au pied du haut siège.

nodes.beat: Under the hall was a stable, warm and dark, and the door at the bottom of the steps would not open until Elsie held up what she had been given on the crossing to keep danger off her; then it swung back as if it knew. In the one stall stood a grey horse with eight legs. He had stood there, shut in, since the morning his master's raven did not come home. His name was Sleipnir. He put his nose down to Muninn and blew very softly, and then he knelt, all eight knees, so that Elsie could climb on.

nodes.role: the open square, crossed in full view

choices.gist: Tu continues à marcher, jusqu'au haut siège.
choices.echo: Elsie atteignit les marches du haut siège, et s'arrêta.

nodes.beat: Elsie walked down the middle of Valhalla with every face in it turned towards her and the stone held up in her fist, shining, the one small sun in the hall. Sköll came down the floor behind her, not hurrying. Nobody stopped him. Nobody stopped her either. It was the longest walk of her life, and she did not look back once.

nodes.role: the long way round, under the wall

choices.gist: Tu sors de l'ombre au pied du haut siège.
choices.echo: Elsie sortit de l'ombre, et l'homme borgne la regardait déjà.

nodes.beat: Elsie went round by the wall, under the hanging shields where the firelight did not reach, with Muninn inside her coat and the stone hidden in her fist. She could hear Sköll coming down the middle of the hall, sniffing, sure of himself. Twice he stopped, and she stopped too and held her breath. At the end of the wall there was only the high seat, and the steps up to it, and the one-eyed man, waiting.

nodes.role: the last hour, and two ways to arrive

choices.gist: Tu montes les marches du haut siège sous les yeux de toute la grande salle, et tu brandis ensemble Muninn et la pierre.
choices.echo: Elsie monta les marches une à une, et tous les guerriers du Valhalla retinrent leur souffle.

choices.gist: Tu te glisses dans l'ombre derrière le haut siège, où sont couchés les deux loups, et tu laisses Sköll venir à toi.
choices.echo: Elsie se baissa derrière le haut siège, entre les deux loups, et ils ne bougèrent pas.

nodes.beat: At the foot of the high seat Elsie stopped. The one-eyed man looked down at her. He was the man from the bench in Museum Gardens and from the gate of the frozen field, and he did not pretend he was not. Sköll was a dozen paces behind her, and the whole hall was silent. The man held out his hand for the raven. He had paid an eye once for what he wanted, he said, and nothing worth having was free, and the wolf would have the stone unless somebody stopped him.

nodes.role: the last scene, met face on
nodes.beat: Elsie stood on the steps of the high seat in front of all Valhalla, with Muninn on one fist and the stone in the other, and Sköll came up the hall for the stone. She did not run. She turned to face him with the one-eyed man at her back, and the light of the stone on the wolf's grey face.

nodes.role: the last scene, met from the dark
nodes.beat: Elsie crouched in the shadow behind the high seat, between the one-eyed man's two sleeping wolves, with Muninn inside her coat and the stone in her fist. Sköll came round the seat after her, slow and sure, following the smell of the sun. When his head came round the corner she stepped out to meet him.

ending.outline: Everything carried does a job and the jobs fit together. It ends the way it was meant to and the walk home is under their own power.

nodes.beat: Everything Elsie had carried did its job, and the jobs fitted together, and Sköll went back out of the west door with nothing, after the sun where he belonged. Muninn went home to its master's shoulder, and the one-eyed man, who was Odin, sent her back to York at dusk on the same Monday with every memory she had, and Grandad calling her name. Two weeks later the stone went into a case in the Yorkshire Museum, with Grandad's name and hers on the label. On the museum roof there was a raven, and it seemed to be remembering something.

ending.outline: One thing short, and the gap shows. It holds anyway, and the cost is paid by something that can be mended.

nodes.beat: One thing short, and it showed, but it held. Sköll went out of the west door with nothing, and Muninn went home. The one-eyed man, who was Odin, kept the stone for his price, and said it was fair: a raven lent for a sun found. Elsie came back to York at dusk on the same Monday with every memory she had. There was nothing to show the coroner, and Grandad laughed about it for a week. Lent, not found, he said, and the next Saturday he took her detecting anyway.

ending.outline: Enough to finish it and not enough to finish it whole. Something is lost on the way that is not coming back.

nodes.beat: Enough to finish it and not enough to finish it whole. Sköll went away with nothing and Muninn went home, and then the one-eyed man, who was Odin, asked his price, as he had once paid his: one memory. Elsie paid it. She came back to York at dusk on the same Monday, and the stone went into a case in the Yorkshire Museum. Something was missing, and she could not have said what, and the passage never says which memory it was.

ending.outline: Two things and a great deal of luck. It ends, and the ending has to be carried afterwards.

nodes.beat: Two things and a great deal of luck. Sköll went out empty and Muninn went home, but the road the one-eyed man, Odin, opened for Elsie ran back through Jorvik, and it did not open again for a whole summer. She lived that summer. When she stepped out onto Ouse Bridge at dusk on the same Monday, Grandad said she looked older, and she did not tell him why. In the Yorkshire Museum there was a runestone with her name on it in sixteen runes, crooked, that nobody could have cut but her.

ending.outline: One thing, and it is only just enough. Everyone is standing at the end except the part of them that set out.

nodes.beat: One thing, and it was only just enough. Sköll went out empty and Muninn went home, and the price the one-eyed man, Odin, asked for it was everything Elsie remembered of the road. She woke in the frozen field with frost on her coat and Grandad bending over her. He asked what she had been saying about ravens. She did not know. Far off a raven called, and she did not look up.

ending.outline: Empty-handed the whole way. It still ends, and it takes everything they had to give to end it.

nodes.beat: Empty-handed the whole way, and it still ended. Muninn went home to the one-eyed man's shoulder, because Elsie gave everything she had to get it there, but Sköll took the stone out of her hand and swallowed it, and went out of the west door with its light inside him. Odin sent her back to York at dusk on the same Monday with nothing round her neck. The next day the sun came up dim, and at noon the whole city stood in a strange brown twilight that nobody could explain. Elsie walked home through it, and she knew.
